content_metadata.description: This video presents a series of tips and tricks for side mount diving, focusing on how to prevent tank twisting and adjust tank positioning. It is primarily informative and practical, demonstrating techniques using close-up shots of the equipment. The underwater footage and upbeat music interspersed throughout create a sense of adventure and excitement.

qAndA.answer: To counter the force of the bungee cord pulling the tank, ensuring it remains in the desired position.
qAndA.question: Why does Brian place his bolt snap at a 45-degree angle?

qAndA.answer: To easily swap out tanks, particularly useful when transitioning between different tank types like aluminum and steel.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the cam strap system Brian demonstrates?

qAndA.answer: It provides an easy point to cut with a knife or shears in case of entanglement.
qAndA.question: How does the paracord system enhance safety in side mount diving?

qAndA.answer: The video is primarily informative and practical, aiming to educate viewers on side mount diving techniques.

students.
And while I was in side mount, the question was raised by another diver that was on
side, several things.
One, how do you adjust or how do you keep your tanks from twisting when you're bungees
wrapped around your post?
And that's a very simple easy fix here.
And I'll show you real quick what I mean by that.
If you take your bungee off your BC itself or as you go to attach and you wrap it around
the post, what that does is pull that tank into this position here.
It causes two things.
One, it's an annoyance that your valve knob actually digs into your side.
The other thing is it blocks the knob.
You can't get to it if you need to feather or anything like that.
So the real simple easy way to fix that is come up here to the top of the valve itself.
And on the back of the valve, we're going to call this zero degrees.
We'll call the post 90 degrees.
And the dead center part, we're going to call this 45.
So at a 45 degree mark, as I draw my hand down, that just happens to be where my bolt
snap is.
And what that allows is as that bungee system, it actually pulling the cylinder this way,
that bolt snap actually pulls the cylinder back into this position.
So it actually keeps both of my cylinders into correct position that I need them.
So let's go back down here to the bolt snap just for a second.
Because I'm going to show you another little neat trick.
If you do a lot of traveling and you side mount dive when you travel and if you transition
from aluminum to steel, a neat little very simple design or system to use is the same
one I've got here, which is just nothing more than a cam strap, a tri-glide bolt snap,
and then a little piece of per cord.
Now I do this for several reasons because I do a lot of traveling guys.
I do a lot of diving when I travel as far as side mount goes.
And I need an easy simple system when I'm on boats to swap over tanks.
So cam straps are very simple.
Pop it loose, put on another tank, you're set ready to go.
But another reason I use this is for adjustability.
So with this per cord here, I've actually got it set up right now just for the dives
that I'm doing around here.
But this is real simple.
It's just a piece of per cord that runs through a loop, girth hitched around a bolt snap there,
but it's adjustable.
If I need to extend the length for whatever reason, maybe I got thicker gloves on or maybe
I'm transitioning from aluminum to steel instead of attaching to my d-ring on my waist
strap, I can actually attach to the d-ring on my butt plate of my wing system or on my
